answer: According to Section 38 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the right of private defence of the body allows for the voluntary causing of death to an assailant if the offence that triggers this right falls under certain specified descriptions. If the offence does not meet these descriptions, as stated in Section 39, the right does not extend to causing death, but may allow for other forms of harm. Therefore, the extension of private defence to causing death is contingent upon the nature of the offence being committed or attempted.
